title: Lois
summary: Lois is a first-generation church figure whose ministry supports the spread, instruction, or organization of the gospel.
historical_context: The setting is the apostolic mission across the eastern Mediterranean, where house churches and travel networks shaped ministry.
ancient_near_east_context: House churches, patronage, trade routes, and Roman civic life frame the background.
literary_context: Acts and the Epistles use Lois to display gospel partnership and ecclesial formation.
covenantal_significance: Lois participates in the nations' inclusion and the building up of the body of Christ.
interpretive_notes: These figures are best read as part of the church's shared mission rather than isolated heroes.
Letters often mention them to show partnership, hospitality, and instruction.
